description:
Capture desktop screenshot, window list, and interactive UI elements.

The text starts with the coordinate contract, e.g. ``Image 1280x800 = screen
2560x1600 at origin (0,0), scale 2.000; input tools take IMAGE pixels of this
frame (monitor=0, max_width=1280)``. Every window rect and element center in
the text is in IMAGE pixels of the returned image, and Click / Move / Scroll /
Type take IMAGE pixels by default — read a point off the image (or the list)
and pass it as-is, with the same monitor/max_width; the server scales it back.

max_width.description: Max image width in pixels. 0=native resolution. Default 1280 to keep images compact.

monitor.description: Monitor to capture. 0=all monitors (default; on macOS the main display), 1/2/3=specific monitor.

name: Snapshot
title: Snapshot

description:
Capture a part of the Snapshot image at native resolution, to read small text.

View only. The rectangle is in IMAGE pixels of the last Snapshot (pass the same
monitor/max_width), cut to that frame. The result is captured at native
resolution and downscaled only when wider than max_width. Input tools keep
taking Snapshot image pixels: to click something seen in the zoom, convert it
with the reply's origin and scale (screen = origin + round(image * scale)) and
pass coords="screen". For a capture wider than 1280 px use max_width=0 with
coords="screen".

coords.description:
'image' (default) or 'screen' = raw OS coordinates (physical pixels
on Windows/Linux, points on macOS).

height.description: Rectangle height, in the same units as y.

max_width.description: max_width of the Snapshot frame, also the widest image returned (0=native).

monitor.description: monitor of the Snapshot frame (default 0, as Snapshot).

width.description: Rectangle width, in the same units as x.

x.description: Left edge in Snapshot image pixels (screen coordinates if coords="screen").

y.description: Top edge in Snapshot image pixels (screen coordinates if coords="screen").

name: Zoom
title: Zoom

description:
List the displays: what each `monitor` value of the screen and input tools means.

One line per display: its index (the tools' monitor=N), name, bounds and origin
in screen coordinates, scale, and whether it is the primary. The first line says
what monitor=0 is on this machine: all monitors on Windows and Linux, the main
display on macOS.
name: DisplayInventory
title: DisplayInventory

description: Where the mouse cursor is, in IMAGE pixels of a Snapshot frame and in screen coordinates.

max_width.description: max_width of the Snapshot frame (default 1280, as Snapshot).

monitor.description: monitor of the Snapshot frame (default 0, as Snapshot).

name: CursorPosition
title: CursorPosition

description:
Mouse click at a point of the Snapshot image.

x/y are IMAGE pixels of the last Snapshot / AnnotatedSnapshot (read them off
the image or its element list); the server maps them to the screen
(screen = origin + round(image * scale), clamped to the frame). Pass the same
monitor/max_width the Snapshot used — the defaults are Snapshot's defaults.

action.description:
'click', 'double', 'triple', 'hover', or 'down' / 'up' = press the
button and leave it down / release it, for a drag in steps: Click 'down',
Move, Click 'up'. A pressed button stays down until its 'up'.

coords.description:
'image' (default) or 'screen' = raw OS coordinates, passed through
unchanged (physical pixels on Windows/Linux, points on macOS).

max_width.description: max_width of the Snapshot frame (default 1280, as Snapshot).

modifiers.description:
Keys held during the action, e.g. 'ctrl', 'ctrl+shift', 'alt', 'win'
('cmd' on macOS). Always released afterwards, also when the click fails.

monitor.description: monitor of the Snapshot frame (default 0, as Snapshot).

x.description: X in Snapshot image pixels (screen coordinates if coords="screen").

y.description: Y in Snapshot image pixels (screen coordinates if coords="screen").

name: Click
title: Click

description:
Type text in any language, optionally clicking a point of the Snapshot image first.

Any Unicode text is typed exactly — diacritics (e.g. Slovak "Žltý kôň
ďakuje"), symbols (€, –) and emoji — whatever the machine's keyboard layout.
"\n" (also "\r\n") presses Enter and "\t" presses Tab. The reply "Typed N
chars" counts the characters handed to the OS. A desktop that cannot take
input (a locked Windows/macOS screen, a secure desktop, no display, a missing
permission) is an error before anything is typed; on Windows, input the OS
refuses part-way is an error saying how many got through, never a success.
x/y are IMAGE pixels of the last Snapshot (see Click); 0/0 = type at the
current focus without clicking.

clear.description: Clear existing content first (select all, Delete).

max_width.description: max_width of the Snapshot frame (default 1280, as Snapshot).

method.description:
'keys' (default) = Unicode keystrokes, the clipboard is not
touched. 'paste' = put the text on the clipboard, press Ctrl+V
(Command+V on macOS), then restore the previous clipboard text — only
for an app that ignores typed keystrokes (some games, nested remote
desktops). Not for secrets: clipboard history keeps a copy. The reply
means the paste keys were pressed, not that the app took the text.

monitor.description: monitor of the Snapshot frame (default 0, as Snapshot).

x.description:
X in Snapshot image pixels. x=0 with y=0 = no click (type at the current
focus); x=0 alone is the left column.

y.description: Y in Snapshot image pixels. y=0 alone is the top row.

name: Type
title: Type

description:
Turn the mouse wheel at a point of the Snapshot image.

amount = mouse-wheel CLICKS (notches), the same unit on Windows, macOS and
Linux; direction = 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right'. Example:
Scroll(amount=3, direction="down") scrolls down by three wheel notches.
x/y are IMAGE pixels of the last Snapshot (see Click); 0/0 = scroll where the
mouse already is.

amount.description:
Wheel clicks, clamped to 1..100. Legacy form (no direction): the
sign picks the direction — positive = up/right, negative = down/left.

direction.description:
'up', 'down', 'left' or 'right'. When given it wins over the
sign of amount and over horizontal.

horizontal.description: Legacy, only without direction: scroll left/right instead of up/down.

max_width.description: max_width of the Snapshot frame (default 1280, as Snapshot).

modifiers.description: Keys held while the wheel turns, e.g. 'ctrl' to zoom. Always released afterwards.

monitor.description: monitor of the Snapshot frame (default 0, as Snapshot).

x.description:
X in Snapshot image pixels. x=0 with y=0 = where the mouse already is;
x=0 alone is the left column.

y.description: Y in Snapshot image pixels. y=0 alone is the top row.

name: Scroll
title: Scroll

description:
Move the mouse, or drag, to a point of the Snapshot image.

x/y and start_x/start_y are IMAGE pixels of the last Snapshot (see Click).

drag.description: If true, drag from start position to target.

max_width.description: max_width of the Snapshot frame (default 1280, as Snapshot).

monitor.description: monitor of the Snapshot frame (default 0, as Snapshot).

start_x.description:
Drag start X in image pixels. start_x=0 with start_y=0 = drag from
the current position; start_x=0 alone is the left column.

start_y.description: Drag start Y in image pixels. start_y=0 alone is the top row.

x.description: Target X in Snapshot image pixels.

y.description: Target Y in Snapshot image pixels.

name: Move
title: Move

description: Execute keyboard shortcut, or press one key several times.

repeat.description: How many times to press it, 1..100.

name: Shortcut
title: Shortcut

description: Hold keys down for a time, then release them. They are released also on a failure.

keys.description: One key or several joined by '+', e.g. 'w', 'shift+w', 'ctrl+alt'.

seconds.description: How long to hold, capped at 30.

name: HoldKey
title: HoldKey

description: Pause execution, without blocking other tools. To wait for something on screen use WaitFor.
name: Wait
title: Wait

description:
Wait until text shows on screen or a window appears; other tools keep working meanwhile.

Checks every 0.5 s and replies with what matched and where. Not found in time
is an error. Matching is case-insensitive and on part of the text or title. Text
is read by OCR: give a short distinctive string, OCR is not exact.

max_width.description: max_width of the Snapshot frame for a window's rect (default 1280, as Snapshot).

text.description: Text to find by OCR. Give exactly one of text and window.

timeout.description: Seconds to keep trying, 0..300 (0 = check once).

window.description: Part of a window title to find.

name: WaitFor
title: WaitFor

description: Bring a window to the foreground.
name: FocusWindow
title: FocusWindow

description: Minimize all windows (Win+D — show desktop).
name: MinimizeAll
title: MinimizeAll

description: Launch, switch to, or resize an application.

height.description: New height (for resize), in the same raw screen units as width.

width.description:
New width (for resize), in raw screen units (the coords="screen" space:
physical pixels on Windows/Linux, points on macOS) — not Snapshot image pixels.

name: App
title: App

description:
Execute a shell command (PowerShell on Windows, zsh on macOS, bash on Linux).

On Windows the command runs unchanged in a console switched to UTF-8 before PowerShell
starts, so PowerShell's output comes back as exact Unicode; error records, exit codes and
``param(...)`` are plain PowerShell's. On macOS/Linux the output is read in the locale's
encoding. On Linux the command also gets the server user's own session variables the
service lacks (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, the D-Bus session bus, DISPLAY), so ``systemctl --user``
works. Start a GUI program detached (``setsid -f prog >/dev/null 2>&1``): a plain
``prog &`` keeps the output open, so the call runs to its timeout and the program is
stopped with it. A prompt (ssh, sudo -A, a locked keyring) may open a dialog on the screen
instead of failing: run it non-interactively (``ssh -o BatchMode=yes``,
``env -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS``).

The text reply is stdout, ``[STDERR] …`` and ``[Exit code: N]``; the structured content has
the exact ``stdout``, ``stderr`` and ``exit_code``, for a client that must not parse text.

cwd.description:
Working directory (spaces and quotes are fine; ~ and $VAR, or %VAR%
on Windows, are expanded). If provided, the command runs inside that
directory; a path that is not an existing directory is an error and
the command does not run.

title: Shell

description:
Reconnect a disconnected Windows desktop session to the console.

This enables screenshot and UI automation tools to work when no RDP
client is actively connected. Runs 'tscon' to attach this server's own
session to the console, then checks it worked. This puts the desktop on the
machine's physical screen. A session that is already attached (console or
remote desktop) is left alone.

force.description: Reconnect even if session appears active (default False).

name: ReconnectSession

name: FileDownload
title: FileDownload

description:
Upload a file from base64-encoded content. Use for binary files.

Over HTTP one request carries at most 4 MiB, so one call carries about 3 MB of file. Send a
larger file in pieces: ``append=False`` first, then ``append=True``, ideally to a temporary
name, checked with FileHash and moved into place with FileRename (``remoteos-call put`` does
exactly that).

append.description: Add to the end of the file instead of replacing it (a missing file is created).

data_base64.description:
Base64-encoded file content, at most 100 MB of base64 text. Line breaks are
allowed; any other character outside the base64 alphabet is an error and nothing is
written.

permissions_from.description:
Without append: start a new file with this existing file's permissions,
so a temporary copy of a private file is private too. A directory here is an error.

name: FileUpload
title: FileUpload

description: The SHA-256 and size of a file: ``sha256:<hex> <size> bytes``. Use it to check a transfer.
name: FileHash
title: FileHash

description:
Rename a file, replacing ``new_path`` in one step if it exists.

The new file takes an existing ``new_path``'s POSIX mode and group (and, when the server runs
as root, its owner), not its ACLs or extended attributes. A symlink there is written through,
a ``new_path`` this account may not write is refused. Both paths must be on the same filesystem.
name: FileRename
title: FileRename

names (root-owned on Linux, reachable with sudo).

ref.description: A commit sha, tag or branch of remoteos-mcp (default main).

description:
Extract text from screen using OCR. Captures a region or the full screen.

Uses pytesseract if available, falls back to platform-specific OCR engine.

The region is in SCREEN coordinates (physical pixels on Windows/Linux, points
on macOS) — NOT Snapshot image pixels.

left.description: Left edge of region (0 = full screen).

name: OCR
title: OCR

description:
Record the screen and return an animated GIF.

The region is in SCREEN coordinates (physical pixels on Windows/Linux, points
on macOS) — NOT Snapshot image pixels.

left.description: Left edge of capture region (0 = full screen).

name: ScreenRecord
title: ScreenRecord

description:
Take a screenshot with numbered labels on interactive UI elements.

Draws red rectangles and white numbered labels on each interactive element,
making it easy for AI agents to identify click targets visually. Same frame and
coordinate contract as Snapshot: the text starts with the contract line, element
centers are IMAGE pixels, and Click / Move / Scroll / Type take them as-is.

Uses the platform accessibility tree for the foreground window (Win32 child
windows on Windows, AT-SPI on Linux X11); returns the plain screenshot with a
note when the focused app exposes no elements.

max_elements.description: Maximum number of elements to annotate (default 30).

max_width.description: Max image width in pixels. 0=native resolution. Default 1280 (same as Snapshot).

monitor.description: Monitor to capture. 0=all monitors (default; on macOS the main display), 1/2/3=specific monitor.
